source: NASA Exoplanet Archive, `pscomppars` (Planetary Systems Composite Parameters), public TAP sync endpoint
attribution: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.
units: vmag in magnitudes; planets is a count
notes: The join column is `gaia_dr3_id`; its values carry a literal "Gaia DR3 " prefix which is stripped before matching. A column named `gaia_id` does not exist and raises ORA-00904.
Match order: Gaia DR3 source_id -> HIP -> HD -> nearest AT-HYG star within 10 arcsec.

`star` is the global index into the l0 ++ l1 concatenation. A host whose star fell into L2 reports tier "l2" and star null, because L2 carries no global index — its has-exoplanet flag bit is still set inside the L2 chunk.

Unmatched hosts are overwhelmingly fainter than V = 10 and therefore outside the AT-HYG m10 subset entirely. They are listed in `unmatchedHosts` as [name, planetCount] so the UI can still show them honestly rather than pretending they do not exist.

schema.matchedHosts: array of { host, planets, star, tier, via, hip?, hd?, vmag? }
schema.unmatchedHosts: array of [hostName, planetCount] — no counterpart in the AT-HYG m10 subset
